news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass has ordered a pause on utility shutoffs through the end of the year for customers who may not be able to pay their bills amid skyrocketing rates.

Bass said she asked the LA Department of Water and Power to take action for Angelenos “facing higher bills after the record heat.”

“No LADWP customer who is unable to pay their residential bill will have their electricity or water turned off for the remainder of this year,” she said in a statement.

“Running our air conditioners has been a necessity, and for too many Angelenos, the resulting increase in utility bills is a real burden,” Bass added.

“Angelenos need swift relief, and I am taking concrete action to provide it,” she added, telling customers to pay what they can afford now.

Bass’s move comes after Canter’s Deli, the nearly 100-year-old Fairfax District institution, warned it may have to cut staff after its LADWP bill jumped nearly $10,000 in four months to more than $34,000.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Let’s play a game of multiple choice. Circle which of the following read true after six weeks of football:

A. The Browns lead the AFC North.

B. The Cardinals beat the vaunted Rams, who are last in the NFC West, without scoring a touchdown.

C. J.J. McCarthy threw for 242 yards in one quarter of football — for the Giants, who have backpedaled into the NFC East lead.

If you chose D, congratulations! You’re either a prophet, or you’re contrarian enough to guess nothing is ever foregone in the NFL.

Favorites may have cruised to a 10-6 mark last week, but the tides still say it’s time to be bold.

If there are any certainties at this stage, it’s that the 49ers are the stoics of football. Even with a litany of injuries, they’ve scrambled to 6-0 with their seasoned veteran core. Besides, teams are figuring out that Michael Penix Jr. folds under duress.

There’s nothing to love about Bo Nix and this arid offense. The defense was to credit for last week’s overtime win over Seattle, and it can swallow a Cardinals team that just went 0-for-6 in the red zone.

Sam Darnold’s turnovers are becoming a problem, and it cost Seattle a win. Patrick Mahomes is back to business as usual this season with a trustworthy offensive line and run game.

The Jets may be 2-4, but they’re hanging in games against anyone, running at 5-1 against the spread. Miami’s rest can’t fix a raw roster that is in over its head every week.

Houston’s passing game is finally humming after an 0-4 start. If McCarthy does start after his fourth-quarter show, stopping a seasoned Houston team on the road is too tall an order.

We didn’t need another game to determine whether Tampa Bay’s upset over the Cowboys was a fluke. It was. Carolina ranks eighth overall in offensive EPA per play, and that’s enough to oust a turnover-prone Tampa attack.

Tip your caps to Tennessee and Cleveland, which both pulled off signature wins. Now they meet as fellow inconsistent passing games, so take the higher scoring profile and late-game execution.

Neither offense has been a pleasure to watch. Aaron Rodgers and an encouraging Pittsburgh ground game can smart their way out of London against the green Saints.

Embarrassment is the theme of this one. There’s simply nothing to like about either of these teams. The Eagles’ free-fall, though, is less adjustable without Jalen Hurts for the rest of the year. While the Cowboys offense has become predictable, its high ceiling can flush out Philadelphia.

Of course, this once again comes down to Lamar Jackson’s status. The offense stalled out with Tyler Huntley in a stale loss to Cleveland. Joe Burrow’s aerial attack can make quick work of them if that continues.

Caleb Williams will return, and that immediately elevates the Bears’ downfield passing and red-zone efficiency. Drake Maye, though he has redeemed himself, has a tall order matching the Bears’ potent offense with more offensive line health problems.

Judging off of preseason expectations, the Raiders have perhaps been the year’s most delightful surprise; the Rams have been the most disappointing. Why stop now?

It’s probably the biggest coin toss of the week. Detroit is tied with Buffalo for the highest point average despite serious third-down issues and a defense that lets everyone pace them. Josh Jacobs returns just in time to a desperate Packers run game as Green Bay is riding three straight wins, so I’ll lean that way.

There’s only so much the Vikings defense can compensate for. Daniel Jones is struggling, but he has the tools to overcome Kyler Murray’s 31st-ranked passing offense.

LAST WEEK: 8-6, 64/105 points

OVERALL: 53-42, 461/769 points

Sean Treppedi handicaps the NFL, NHL, MLB and college football for the New York Post. He primarily focuses on picks that reflect market value while tracking trends to mitigate risk.

news.title: The political ads that don’t look like ads
news.originalSummary:
The political ads that don’t look like ads

Political campaigns and lobby groups in the US are paying content creators as little as $25 to influence the midterms with social videos. But the system is so opaque that you likely won’t even know you’ve been targeted. Al Jazeera’s Mohammad Qasem looks at how this cheap, fast and viral strategy works.

Thanks to a viral marketing campaign based out of California called “Nixonmaxxing,” former President Richard Nixon is cool now — and surprisingly, that might actually be a good thing.

Look, let’s be real — it is totally bizarre that the president who gave us the Watergate scandal and notoriously resigned in disgrace is suddenly the toast of Instagram.

But — in this age of social media brainrot — if young people find themselves inspired to learn more about history and all its tangled complexities, then I’m all for it.

Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

To return to square one — Richard Nixon was never cool, not even when he was president.

He was so uncool, during the first televised presidential debate in 1960 with JFK, that his sweaty mug famously lost him the razor-thin election.

After he lost the 1962 California gubernatorial race, seemingly dooming his political career, he said, “You won’t have old Nixon to kick around anymore.”

Now Nixon has the kicks. Or as the young people say, “aura.”

“Tricky Dick” is making inroads with Gen Z through wildly popular videos of the 37th president’s speeches set to hip hop tracks — and a sick merch game.

It’s an ingenious marketing campaign by the Nixon Foundation, the Yorba Linda, California-based nonprofit that jointly administers the Nixon Library and Museum alongside the National Archives and Records Administration, the federal agency that operates most presidential libraries.

The vanguard of the campaign is a souvenir ballcap labeled with the chin-scratching term, which plays into the “looksmaxxing” trend.

(The hat has sold out multiple times).

And their account’s top video has cracked 1.4 million views.

Even Vice President JD Vance has wanted in on the Nixon action. In a July visit to the library, he suggested Dick’s legacy was experiencing a “renaissance.”

The allure of Nixonmaxxing spoke to me on a different level.

I had long been interested in how presidential libraries act as rehabilitation projects for a president’s legacy, often to a fault.

In 2022, I visited the Truman Library and was perplexed by the museum’s equivocation when it tried to explain why Truman decided to drop atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, effectively copping out by suggesting, well, it wasn’t really his decision at all.

The Nixon Library suffers from some of the same evasions. The museum’s opening video almost entirely omits Watergate.

Instead, it emphasizes Nixon’s accomplishments that many Americans, progressives included, would cite as positive developments.

He founded the Environmental Protection Agency — and the Endangered Species Act — at the height of the environmental movement.

He signed Title IX to promote equality for women in high school and college sports.

He helped desegregate schools in the South that had thus far resisted the 1954 ruling of Brown v. Board of Education.

He returned Blue Lake, a sacred place in New Mexico to the Taos Native Americans, to the Taos Pueblo’s tribal jurisdiction.

He opened diplomatic relations with the People’s Republic of China, which definitely changed the world, for better or worse.

But the Vietnam War? That wasn’t his fault. That was LBJ’s.

Nixon definitely had a hand — and made key decisions — in Vietnam.

Real history is messy and doesn’t conform to one narrow narrative. The deeper you look, the more you find out that people were complicated.

And the times they lived in — they were as confusing and complicated as the times we live in now.

So even though I can’t get down with treating Nixon with the uncritical glam his library’s social media account endows him with — resurfacing campaign posters that present Tricky Dick’s frumpy face as if he was the 1970s version of Jacob Elordi — I think Nixonmaxxing’s potential in terms of spurring educational curiosity is terrific.

It’s getting young people interested in history.

Right now, in a world where education is mired in AI slop, a viral video might just be the gateway drug into actually reading a book.

Or even inspiring a career of civic service.

The study of history is the practice of interrogating stories, evaluating competing sources and providing a balanced assessment.

For its part, the Nixon Library and Museum does acknowledge Watergate. It has a whole wing devoted to the scandal.

And if that isn’t enough, there have been entire libraries of books written about that mysterious break-in, just waiting for the curious mind to crack them open.

That’s the real Nixonmaxxing — taking on the lessons, and scandals, of history head-on.

To paraphrase the philosopher George Santayana, we need a young generation to engage with history so that they can figure out how not to repeat it.

And maybe, in 2026, that starts with pressing “like” on a Nixon meme.

Harrison Blackman is an editorial assistant at The California Post.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

The bar is low, but Derek Mason and Middle Tennessee State can take a significant step forward as a program on Tuesday against FIU.

After back-to-back 3-9 campaigns to start his tenure in Murfreesboro, Mason and the Blue Raiders are sitting at 3-3 after six games in 2026. A win against the Panthers would not only clinch the best season for Middle Tennessee State under Mason, but it would also get them within striking distance of their first bowl bid since 2022.

Mason has never had a winning season in his nine-year career as a head coach.

There’s a lot on the line for the Blue Raiders, but they’re going to be up against it. MTSU is a 10.5-point underdog for this midweek clash.

This is a tricky spot for FIU. The Panthers lost a heartbreaker on a last-minute field goal to Jacksonville State last week, and now they’ll need to bounce back at Pitbull Stadium against a team that should be feeling good about itself after a 33-30 win over Delaware in Week 7.

That was easily Middle Tennessee’s best performance of the season, but the Blue Raiders will be hard-pressed to repeat that offensive outburst against FIU.

The Panthers struggled to stop Jacksonville State last time out, but that was an outlier compared to the rest of FIU’s defensive performances. The Panthers rank 12th in the country in yards per play allowed (4.4), and they rank 15th in yards per pass allowed (6.0). That latter number is crucial, as Middle Tennessee’s passing game got going against the Blue Hens last week.

Middle Tennessee’s numbers pale in comparison across the board, but the Blue Raiders’ defense should stand a chance against an FIU offense that leaves plenty to be desired. The Panthers’ offense ranks 119th in SP+, and their 5.1 yards per play is good enough for 96th in FBS.

FIU’s defense probably will prove to be too much for Middle Tennessee State, which means over bettors would be relying on the Panthers to do the heavy lifting to get to the window. That seems like a lot to ask from this tepid offense.

The Play: Under 45.5 points (-110, DraftKings)

Kylie Jenner’s $50 million Fantasy Bra was followed by a sparkling second act at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show after-party Sunday night.

The Kylie Cosmetics founder, 29, changed into a crystal-studded underwire bra for the bash. She styled it with black bottoms and her go-to pear-shaped diamond earrings.

On Monday, YouTuber Gigi Gorgeous shared a photo of herself with Jenner and nightlife entrepreneur Marsha Molinari from the Chateau Marmont fête, captioning it, “the angels and icons were out last night👼🏼✨.”

Hours earlier, Jenner made a surprise runway debut in the brand’s first Fantasy Bra since 2018. Its $50 million price tag makes it the most valuable in the tradition’s history, more than triple the $15 million Gisele Bündchen’s Red Hot Fantasy Bra commanded in 2000.

The piece contains more than 4,400 diamonds weighing 1,373.39 carats in total, anchored by a 75.54-carat yellow diamond. Fifteen artisans spent over 1,000 hours assembling its 3,218 individually designed pieces.

“For me, it had to be about the diamonds, the light and the movement,” Jacob & Co. founder Jacob Arabo said in a statement.

Jenner’s boyfriend, Timothée Chalamet, and her mom, Kris Jenner, cheered from the audience at Sony Pictures Studios in Culver City, California.

Sister Kendall Jenner, who walked the show in 2015, 2016 and 2018, wasn’t in attendance Sunday. Still, a source exclusively told Page Six the supermodel thought Kylie “absolutely killed it.”

Kylie’s love of all things bedazzled is well documented. For her 29th birthday in August, she threw a “princess kitty” bash at her Beverly Hills home, complete with bejeweled cocktail cups and a gem-covered cake.

Her sparkly archive also includes a crystal-covered vintage Chanel bikini and a Swarovski-studded LaBourjoisie set she wore for her 21st birthday.

Fellow Victoria’s Secret regulars, including Irina Shayk, Bella Hadid, Tate McRae and Ashley Graham, kept the lingerie theme going after hours.

news.originalContent:
Only 1.4 percent of all new wealth created between 2019 and 2025 went to the poorest 50 percent of the population, report finds.

The top 1 percent in Peru captured 42 percent of all new wealth generated between 2019 and 2025, an analysis by the nonprofit group Oxfam has found.

The report, released on Tuesday, highlights growing inequality in the South American country and raises questions about how the government is addressing deepening social divisions.

“Economic inequality in Peru has remained stubbornly high for decades. And when people feel that the same people always win, that nothing changes and nothing can change, inequality starts to look less like an injustice and more like the natural order of things,” said Alejandra Alayza, the executive director of Oxfam in Peru.

“That is a dangerous kind of fatalism, and we must tear it down.”

The nonprofit told Al Jazeera in an email that the 42 percent figure represents an increase from the 2000 to 2019 period, when the top 1 percent captured about 39 percent of all new wealth.

Just 1.4 percent of new wealth from 2019 to 2025 went to the poorest 50 percent of the country’s population, according to the group.

Experts warn the trend bodes poorly for public faith in government and democratic institutions.

Oxfam worked with the Institute for Peruvian Studies, a think tank in Lima, to publish a report this month on Peruvians’ perceptions of inequality in their country.

The groups found that 84 percent of Peruvians believed their country is governed by powerful interests that shape politics to their benefit. More than 75 percent also said that wealthy corporations and individuals avoid paying their fair share of taxes.

The survey also suggested that public opinion was in favour of action to address the issue.

About 70 percent of respondents said they want the government to do more to reduce inequality, which a majority felt had limited access to services such as healthcare, employment, education and justice.

“The undeniable scale of public support for action to reduce inequality leaves no room for complacency,” Alayza said.

“Inequality is not a force of nature; it is made by political choices. And different choices can build a different Peru.”

Peru’s rising inequality has been accompanied by a period of political turmoil, particularly in the presidential palace.

A stream of probes, scandals and impeachments has led to Peru being governed by nine presidents in the last 10 years.

The latest, right-wing President Keiko Fujimori, was sworn into office in July after a narrow race that saw voting delays and heated recriminations among the leading candidates.

Experts believe powerful interests have found opportunity amid the political tumult.

“It’s sort of a paradox. How can you have such a rotation among elites but still have a relatively narrow political-criminal-business elite that holds a lot of power? I think both things are true in Peru,” Will Freeman, a fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, a US-based think tank, told Al Jazeera.

Part of the political upheaval has come from clashes between the presidency and Peru’s powerful Congress, which has the power to impeach executive leaders on the basis of “moral incapacity”, an ambiguous term.

The repeated leadership shakeups have weakened Peru’s democracy, according to analysts.

In December 2022, for instance, then-President Pedro Castillo announced that he would illegally dissolve Congress in response to repeated attempts to impeach him.

His subsequent removal and arrest prompted widespread protests. The government of Castillo’s successor, Dina Boluarte, implemented a months-long crackdown on the demonstrations that rights groups say included widespread abuses for which there has been little accountability.

In the years since, the Peruvian government has also taken steps to weaken judicial oversight and hollow out anticorruption watchdogs.

The nonprofit Freedom House, which measures political freedom in countries around the world, ranked Peru as “free” in 2022. But its ranking dropped the following year to “partly free”, in light of the deadly clashes between security forces and protesters.

In its 2026 report, Freedom House maintained that Peru was only “partly free”, citing in part the denial of full political rights to certain groups, including Indigenous peoples.

“High-profile corruption scandals have eroded public trust in government, and the weakening of judicial independence has impacted the country’s governing bodies,” the nonprofit said.

Powerful interests, both licit and illicit, have taken advantage of those changes.

“The groups themselves are unstable and fluid,” said Freeman. “And yet, I think Peruvians are right to conclude that, generally, they are wielding outsized influence in defence of their own commercial interests or political power rather [than] in service of some kind of general welfare.”

news.originalContent:
Brazil’s left-wing president says he will release bank, tax, and phone records if right-wing rival will do the same.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has challenged right-wing candidate Senator Flavio Bolsonaro to release his personal records in the run-up to the second round of the country’s presidential election, in which corruption has emerged as a key issue.

Lula said on Tuesday that he would share his bank, tax and telephone records, along with those of his family, if Bolsonaro would agree to do the same.

“I’m willing to let Brazilians see who the thieves and corrupt people in this country really are. I want to see whether he [Bolsonaro] has the courage to disclose his bank and phone records,” the left-wing president said during a campaign event in Maranhao state.

The call from Lula comes as both campaigns try to navigate the fallout of an explosive corruption scandal involving disgraced banker Daniel Vorcaro that has implicated influential individuals and institutions across Brazil.

While Bolsonaro is the only major presidential candidate with direct links to Vorcaro, the scandal has also hit the country’s Supreme Federal Court, a major target of right-wing ire for sentencing former President Jair Bolsonaro, Flavio’s father, to 27 years in prison for his role in a coup plot after Lula defeated him in 2022.

Concerns about corruption have become a potent issue that the right has sought to capitalise on, a dynamic that Lula has tried to turn to his advantage in the closing weeks of the race.

Worries about US interference have also loomed over the race following a series of interventions by the Trump administration in Brazilian domestic matters, and reports that the US social media giant Meta had taken steps to restrict Lula’s online campaign prompted a legal complaint.

The company told Brazil’s Supreme Court on Tuesday that it has taken steps to ensure equal treatment for both candidates.

Meta added that any automated restrictions on advertising accounts from either campaign would be reviewed within two hours through the second round of voting on Sunday.

The news service AFP reported that Lula would seek to disqualify Bolsonaro’s campaign on the grounds that “algorithmic manipulation” in his favour by Meta, citing an anonymous source.
news.content:
Brazil’s left-wing president says he will release bank, tax, and phone records if right-wing rival will do the same.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has challenged right-wing candidate Senator Flavio Bolsonaro to release his personal records in the run-up to the second round of the country’s presidential election, in which corruption has emerged as a key issue.

Lula said on Tuesday that he would share his bank, tax and telephone records, along with those of his family, if Bolsonaro would agree to do the same.

“I’m willing to let Brazilians see who the thieves and corrupt people in this country really are. I want to see whether he [Bolsonaro] has the courage to disclose his bank and phone records,” the left-wing president said during a campaign event in Maranhao state.

The call from Lula comes as both campaigns try to navigate the fallout of an explosive corruption scandal involving disgraced banker Daniel Vorcaro that has implicated influential individuals and institutions across Brazil.

While Bolsonaro is the only major presidential candidate with direct links to Vorcaro, the scandal has also hit the country’s Supreme Federal Court, a major target of right-wing ire for sentencing former President Jair Bolsonaro, Flavio’s father, to 27 years in prison for his role in a coup plot after Lula defeated him in 2022.

Concerns about corruption have become a potent issue that the right has sought to capitalise on, a dynamic that Lula has tried to turn to his advantage in the closing weeks of the race.

Worries about US interference have also loomed over the race following a series of interventions by the Trump administration in Brazilian domestic matters, and reports that the US social media giant Meta had taken steps to restrict Lula’s online campaign prompted a legal complaint.

The company told Brazil’s Supreme Court on Tuesday that it has taken steps to ensure equal treatment for both candidates.

Meta added that any automated restrictions on advertising accounts from either campaign would be reviewed within two hours through the second round of voting on Sunday.

The news service AFP reported that Lula would seek to disqualify Bolsonaro’s campaign on the grounds that “algorithmic manipulation” in his favour by Meta, citing an anonymous source.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images)

Senate Democrats’ top campaign spending arm planned to spend $1.2 million in deep red Mississippi Tuesday while their candidate performed well in the polls.

The Senate Majority PAC intends to air the new television advertisement in support of Democratic Mississippi Senate nominee Scott Colom ahead of his race against Republican Mississippi Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, The Associated Press first reported. The ad is set to start Wednesday and air through Election Day.

“Senate Majority PAC has been watching this race closely, and it is clear Colom is running a competitive race that has put Hyde-Smith on her heels,” the PAC’s spokesperson Lauren French said.

Senate Majority PAC (D) announces its first spending in Mississippi It’ll start a $1.2 million TV ad campaign there Wednesday through Election Day, per an SMP spox #MSSEN

A Wedgwood Polls survey found Colom trailing Hyde-Smith 52% to 48%, while other polls found Hyde-Smith leading by single digits. Mississippi last elected a Democratic U.S. senator in November 1982 and both its Senate seats have been controlled by Republicans since 1989. (RELATED: Ranchers Say Trump’s Beef Imports Have GOP Senator Mike Rounds ‘Treading Water’ In South Dakota)

President Donald Trump won 60.9% of the vote in Mississippi during the 2024 presidential election.

Only $8 million has been spent in the Senate race, with Colom outspending Hyde-Smith nearly $4.6 million to $3.2 million, The Associated Press reported.

Colom campaigned with Democratic Georgia Sen. Raphael Warnock and is scheduled to rally with former Vice President Kamala Harris on Thursday.

The Democratic candidate centered his campaign around affordability, which is the top issue for voters in the election cycle, according to his campaign website. He is also district attorney for Mississippi’s 16th Judicial District, giving him name recognition.

The U.S. Supreme Court ruled in May that Louisiana’s racially gerrymandered map was unconstitutional, prompting the Mississippi state Legislature considered redistricting to redraw black majority districts. The Mississippi state Legislature initially planned to redraw Mississippi’s lone majority-black district, although Republican Mississippi Gov. Tate Reeves canceled a planned special legislative session on redistricting in May after receiving backlash from constituents.

Charles Taylor, executive director of the Mississippi state conference of the NAACP, said rising costs motivated Democratic voters across the state, according to The Washington Post. He highlighted how the U.S. Supreme Court’s decision mobilized black voters.

Thousands of protesters rallied in Jackson to protest the redistricting efforts and mobilized people to vote in November, according to Mississippi Today, a local outlet. Black voters make up roughly 35% of Mississippi’s voting population, according to The Washington Post.

The Senate Majority PAC launched a $5 million television ad campaign in Kansas, a state that has not had a Democratic senator since 1939. It also spent tens of millions in Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska.

Democrats pulled spending from Georgia and North Carolina while Democratic Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff and former Democratic North Carolina Gov. Roy Cooper held comfortable leads.

Republican PACs spent over $326 million to support Republican Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton while he fell behind Democratic Texas Senate nominee James Talarico. It spent $14 million to support Republican Kansas Sen. Roger Marshall and $5 million for Republican South Carolina Sen. Darline Graham.

Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial nominee David Crowley personally approved millions of dollars in county funding for his wife’s employer before seeking guidance from the Milwaukee County Ethics Board about another agreement, records reviewed by the Daily Caller show.

Crowley’s signature appears on a series of contract approvals that increased Milwaukee Count
news.originalContent:
(Photo by Scott Olson/Getty Images)

Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial nominee David Crowley personally approved millions of dollars in county funding for his wife’s employer before seeking guidance from the Milwaukee County Ethics Board about another agreement, records reviewed by the Daily Caller show.

Crowley’s signature appears on a series of contract approvals that increased Milwaukee County’s financial commitment to Community Advocates, a nonprofit employing his wife, Ericka Crowley, from $6.5 million to $17.85 million between 2020 and 2021.

Crowley, who became Milwaukee County Executive in May 2020, wrote to the Ethics Board in May 2021 about an upcoming rental assistance contract with Community Advocates, where his wife had begun working the previous year. (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: Dem Candidate Approved Tens Of Millions To His Wife’s Employer While In Office)

“Community Advocates was chosen as a community partner and vendor for the disbursement of Rental Assistance Funding due to the long-standing ties between Milwaukee County and their organization, their commitment to serving our communities, and their competency in administering vital programs like this one,” Crowley wrote in the letter reviewed by the Caller.

“My wife’s employment did not in any way influence the decision to award Community Advocates, and we have had many contracts with the organization — including a prior contract to disburse a previous tranche of Rental Assistance Funding — that were initiated and executed prior to my wife joining their organization as an employee,” he continued.

Crowley said he submitted the letter to maintain “full transparency.”

MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 06: Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Crowley is embraced by his wife Ericka following a campaign event

But while Crowley emphasized the county’s longstanding relationship with Community Advocates, records show he personally approved three increases to the nonprofit’s contract after his wife joined the organization.

Community Advocates originally received a $6.5 million contract in July 2020, just months after Crowley assumed office.

Crowley approved a $5 million increase on Nov. 25, 2020, bringing the contract’s total value to $11.5 million.

He approved another $950,000 increase on Jan. 12, 2021, bringing the total to $12.45 million.

On March 1, 2021, Crowley approved a third increase of $5.4 million, raising the agreement’s total value to $17.85 million and extending the contract through December 2021. (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: Dem Candidate Oversaw Contract With Soros-Linked Group Aimed At ‘Advancing Racial Justice’)

Crowley had previously disclosed his wife’s employment in an economic-interest statement received by Milwaukee County on Jan. 28, 2021, according to Wisconsin Public Radio.

But while that filing disclosed the financial relationship, it did not establish whether Crowley had sought ethics guidance on his personal involvement in approving funding for his wife’s employer.

Crowley had already approved two contract increases before the disclosure was received and signed off on another $5.4 million increase in March, more than two months before contacting the Ethics Board about an upcoming agreement.

In his May letter, Crowley said he had consulted Milwaukee County Corporation Counsel, which advised that the upcoming contract was permissible. The letter did not indicate whether he had obtained similar guidance before approving the earlier funding increases.

The county awarded the original contract without competitive bidding under emergency procurement procedures during the COVID-19 pandemic, Wisconsin Public Radio reported.

Crowley’s campaign told WPR, “Community Advocates launched their rent help program on April 1, before David was even County Executive.”

“When the county’s pandemic relief money came in, it plugged into the program that was already working, run by a partner the county had trusted for over two decades under Republicans and Democrats alike,” Crowley campaign spokesperson Philip Shulman said. “Every dollar was approved by the County Board in public, and David went above and beyond to disclose.”

Since Crowley assumed office in 2020, Milwaukee County distributed more than $65 million in federal Emergency Rental Assistance funds through its partnership with Community Advocates.

Crowley’s campaign did not respond to a request for comment from the Daily Caller.

Crowley will face off against Republican gubernatorial nominee and current Wisconsin Rep. Tom Tiffany in the general election on Nov. 3.

news.originalContent:
The death was added to the federal tally, as the US records more than 4,400 measles cases nationwide.

The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) has reported that a third person has died due to measles in the United States, as the country grapples with its largest measles outbreak in decades.

The CDC did not specify on Tuesday in which state the death occurred. The agency’s national tally remains lower than the number of measles-related deaths reported by state officials, particularly in Pennsylvania, the state hardest hit by the outbreak. Pennsylvania had reported 1,286 cases and five deaths as of Monday.

The CDC confirmed a death on Tuesday after the National Center for Health Statistics verified that measles was listed as the underlying cause of death on a death certificate.

The CDC reported 4,410 measles cases nationwide as of October 15. The agency has said its death count could change as further reviews are completed. The outbreak in Pennsylvania has spread well beyond its initial epicentre in Lancaster County, with 42 counties now reporting cases.

The federal government’s approach to counting measles deaths has drawn scrutiny after the CDC shifted to relying on mortality data from the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) rather than state health departments’ reports.

The CDC has previously told Al Jazeera that it is working with the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists to establish a standardised definition for measles deaths. In the meantime, they will use NCHS mortality data as their measure.

news.originalContent:
A 24-year-old man, who was already being held in quarantine, is the latest to test positive, according to the Health Ministry.

Kenya on high alert amid concern over screening after first Ebola death

⁠Kenya has confirmed ⁠a new Ebola case, bringing the total ‌number of infections in the country to ⁠nine, amid an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), raising concerns about a regional spread.

A 24-year-old man, who was already being held in quarantine, is the latest to test positive, Kenya’s Ministry of Health said in a statement on Tuesday.

“He was isolated at the first sign of illness, tested and started on treatment immediately upon confirmation of his positive test result,” it said, adding he “was already in quarantine when he fell ill”.

The man was a close family member of Kenya’s first Ebola patient, who had travelled from the DRC, through Uganda and before arriving in Kenya and dying at a Nairobi hospital on ⁠October 5.

“All nine cases belong to one cluster, and as of ‌today there is no evidence of transmission outside this group,” Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth said in a statement on Tuesday.

“Eight patients are stable and responding well to treatment, while 134 of 135 contacts have been traced and quarantined,” Amoth said.

Amoth said a milestone was in sight for the majority of the contacts in quarantine as they had remained well for the 21-day monitoring period and could return home from October 25.

It appealed to communities to welcome them back, saying they “pose no risk of infection”.

The ministry said no infections had occurred within quarantine facilities and that it was continuously monitoring infection-prevention measures to protect health workers.

Despite the nine infections, Kenya has not imposed restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings, with authorities saying the country remains open for business.

In the DRC, there have been more than 9,000 Ebola cases and 4,000 deaths since May.

The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control says it’s the second-largest epidemic on record.

It has been difficult to contain because there is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment for the Bundibugyo strain of the virus.

در ابتدا هفت مرد در چارچوب تحقیقات پلیس مبارزه با تروریسم بازداشت شدند که بعدا با قرار وثیقه آزاد شدند.

پنج مرد در سه ون در نزدیکی پایگاه با بنزین پیدا شدند. آنها ابتدا به ظن ارتکاب تخلف بر اساس قانون مواد منفجره بازداشت شدند و سپس به ظن آماده‌سازی برای انجام یک اقدام تروریستی بار دیگر بازداشت شدند.

بازداشت‌های مجددی که امروز (سه‌شنبه) اعلام شد، مربوط به مرد ۲۴ ساله‌ای است که ابتدا در ۲۷ سپتامبر در نزدیکی پایگاه بازداشت شده بود و همچنین مرد ۲۵ ساله‌ای که چند روز بعد، در اول اکتبر، در وست‌مینستر به ظن آماده‌سازی اقدامات تروریستی بازداشت شده بود.

پنج مرد دیگر همچنان با قرار وثیقه پلیس آزاد هستند.

لارنس تیلور، معاون کمیسر پلیس و رئیس پلیس مبارزه با تروریسم بریتانیا، گفت: «این تحقیقات همچنان به‌طور جدی ادامه دارد و ما به جمع‌آوری شواهد ادامه می‌دهیم، اما در حال حاضر موضع ما تغییری نکرده است؛ ما دخالت دولت ایران را بسیار محتمل می‌دانیم.»

او افزود: «بازرسان ما همچنان در حال بررسی میزان این دخالت و هدف پشت آن هستند.»

این مقام پلیس گفت که تحقیقات مربوط به امنیت ملی، به دلیل ماهیت حساسیتشان، ممکن است به زمان نیاز داشته باشند.

او گفت: «تیم‌های تخصصی ما بی‌وقفه تلاش کرده‌اند تا مسیرهای متعدد تحقیقاتی را در این پرونده بسیار پیچیده بررسی کنند.»

در پی این حادثه که در ساعات اولیه روز ۲۷ سپتامبر (۵ مهر) رخ داد، بسیاری از مقام‌های بریتانیا از جمله اندی برنام،‌ نخست‌وزیر و کن مک‌کالم، رئیس ام‌آی۵ (سازمان اطلاعات داخلی بریتانیا) حکومت ایران و سپاه پاسداران را متهم به ارتباط با این حادثه کردند.

پس از این اتهام ایران و بریتانیا سفرای یکدیگر را احضار کرده و مراتب اعتراض خود را ابلاغ کردند.

news.title: As Macron visits Gulf, can France forge its own energy-for-security future?

news.originalContent:
President Macron’s Gulf visit aims to address rising energy prices and strengthen ties amid regional security concerns.

President Emmanuel Macron has arrived in Bahrain during his tour of the Gulf region, as France continues to reel from a wave of violent protests.

The French leader is hoping to strengthen defence ties and secure oil and gas supplies amid major disruption to global fuel shipments arising from the US-Israel war on Iran. He has already visited Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) as part of his three-day trip. His next stop is Qatar.

On the first day of Macron’s trip, France and Kuwait signed eight agreements and cooperation documents covering defence, artificial intelligence, investment and more.

Macron then met UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Abu Dhabi on Monday. The two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to advancing cooperation in energy, advanced technology and artificial intelligence (AI).

According to the French Foreign Ministry, the UAE is France’s biggest importer in the Gulf, with bilateral trade standing at 10.8 billion euros ($12.1bn) in 2025. According to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) [PDF], France supplied 18 percent of the UAE’s arms and defence imports in 2025 – the second highest after the United States, at 42 percent.

But this isn’t all about simple trade.

Andreas Krieg, a senior lecturer at King’s College London’s School of Security Studies, explained that Macron’s visit to the region is “symptomatic of a much larger geopolitical transformation”.

“We are witnessing the gradual emergence of a post-American Middle East in which Washington remains militarily powerful but increasingly struggles to exercise the political leadership it once enjoyed,” Krieg told Al Jazeera.

“Europe and the Gulf now face a remarkably similar strategic challenge. Both have become excessively dependent on American security decisions, and both are discovering that this dependence carries substantial economic and political costs.”

Most pressing for Macron is finding solutions for strife at home.

France has been engulfed in protests and violence over a proposed government budget seeking tens of millions of euros in savings to public spending. Protesters angry about the crumbling state of French schools and planned pay freezes for public-sector workers have taken to the streets in increasingly violent protests, and authorities have imposed curfews in some cities.

More than half a million people gathered across France on Saturday as protesters demanded better education infrastructure and government steps to address the cost-of-living crisis. During weeks of protests, more than 2,500 people have been arrested, and demonstrations have descended into looting and arson in numerous locations.

A major issue is the spike in energy prices affecting all of Europe – much of it as a result of the Iran war – which has also fuelled growing public anger in France. Disruptions to the supply of refined oil products such as petrol and diesel caused by the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz have caused up to 20 percent of French petrol stations to run out of both at various times since the conflict began.

Macron’s visit to the Gulf, accompanied by senior executives from France’s two biggest energy groups, TotalEnergies and Engie, comes as oil prices hover above $100 a barrel.

What France needs most urgently, therefore, is new suppliers. Those look to have been secured.

On Tuesday, the UAE committed to supplying 100,000 tonnes (746,000 barrels) of diesel per month to France for an unspecified duration, according to Bloomberg.

Bahrain has agreed to supply 100,000 tonnes of diesel per month for an unspecified duration, while Saudi Arabia will provide 95,000 tonnes in each of October and November, via TotalEnergies.

Besides securing oil imports, however, France is also looking to boost its own exports, particularly of its defence equipment to the Gulf region, as the country suffers from record national debt – the highest level since the immediate aftermath of World War II, analysts say.

France has already strengthened its military partnership with Saudi Arabia, which has been battling the Iran-backed Houthi group from Yemen.

Last month, Macron said France would send troops and defence systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port of Yanbu, which is crucial for energy transport. Oil installations and airports in Saudi Arabia have come under attack from the Houthi group.

In late September, Macron said France would deploy what he termed “military means” to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Yanbu Red Sea oil terminal. Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, which carries oil from its eastern oilfields across the Arabian Peninsula to the Red Sea, has come under attack during the Iran conflict. It is the country’s main means of continuing to export oil while the critical Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted. But Yemen’s Houthis have also been attacking Saudi ships in the Red Sea.

Macron stated in a TV interview that “soldiers, radars, defence systems” would be sent.

While he did not give specifics about volumes, it was a move described by French newspaper Le Monde as marking “a geopolitical shift”, as defence cooperation between the two countries has previously been “discreet, ambiguous and marked by extreme caution when it came to defining it”, the newspaper noted.

Last week, France’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Pascal Confavreux, said again that “operational elements” to defend Saudi oil facilities had been put into action, without specifying which “military means” had been sent.

Meanwhile, on Monday, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot met with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, to review bilateral relations and discuss regional developments. Barrot also reaffirmed France’s solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks.

Krieg assesses that France can offer Gulf states generally something that has become “increasingly valuable”: military capabilities not entirely dependent on the US.

“France can offer defence industrial cooperation, technology transfers, joint production, training and greater operational autonomy,” he said. “For countries such as the UAE and Qatar, this means progressively reducing their dependence on American weapons systems, spare parts, intelligence and political permissions.”

However, Krieg cautioned that the “central strategic dilemma” for France is likely to be whether increasing its involvement in the region could draw it into the ongoing conflict.

“Consider the protection of Saudi energy infrastructure against Houthi attacks,” he said. “French air defence systems intercepting missiles would directly undermine the Houthis’ military strategy. If French forces are subsequently targeted, Paris could face pressure to retaliate. What begins as a defensive deployment could gradually become an operational commitment with much wider implications.”

Krieg explained that the same is likely to apply to naval deployments around the Strait of Hormuz, adding that “escalation in one theatre can rapidly affect another”.

France’s ties with Iran have already been strained over tit-for-tat diplomatic expulsions and political rhetoric against each other.

In July and August, France strongly condemned Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

In July, two French Embassy staff members were detained in Tehran and then declared personae non gratae. Iran’s Foreign Ministry said the diplomats had “interfered in Iran’s internal affairs under the pretext of engaging with civil society”.

In August, French Foreign Minister Barrot expelled two Iranian diplomats in retaliation.

Speaking at the Global Security Forum in the Qatari capital, Doha, on Tuesday, US Envoy Tom Barrack said that Washington is moving away from its traditional security-for-oil relationship with the Middle East and no longer seeks to dominate the region.

“The US no longer wants to own,” said Barrack, who serves as US ambassador to Turkiye and special envoy for Syria. “The bargain is not to control, but to not leave. We’re not leaving.”

Barrack acknowledged that, following months of Iranian strikes on their infrastructure, regional partners are increasingly recognising the limits of US involvement.

Across the Middle East itself, defence partnerships have grown. In August, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan signed a trilateral security pact, also known as the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement. The pact has been activated amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

But there may now be an opening for other external actors – such as France – to find more of a role.

Krieg said Gulf states do not believe France will replace the US, whose military and intelligence infrastructure remains “unmatched”. Rather, they want a “diversified network of security partnerships”.

“France is particularly attractive because it possesses genuine expeditionary capabilities and has demonstrated a willingness to defend Gulf partners without joining Washington’s offensive campaign against Iran,” he said. “Its military presence has consequently acquired greater political significance.”

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Samuel Corum/Getty Images)

A political ad-style video showing Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton’s “abusive and estranged” biological mother drew condemnation on social media, with critics accusing her Republican opponent, Vivek Ramaswamy, of engaging in a sleazy attack.

The video featured Acton’s estranged mother, Donna Arthur, describing her daughter as a “liar,” disputing allegations about her upbringing and urging Ohioans not to vote for her. Acton’s campaign responded in a statement Tuesday.

🚨 BREAKING OVERNIGHT: In a huge surprise, Amy Acton’s own MOTHER just went on camera urging Ohioans NOT to vote for her daughter for governor "My name is Donna Arthur and I’m Amy Acton’s mother…Amy has a serious problem. She is a liar. She lies about her past. She says she grew up living in a tent. None of that is true." “My daughter needs help…Don’t vote for people who lie. Don’t let her become your governor. If you think she’ll make your life better, you’re fooling yourself. It will only get worse.” 🤯🤯 Now her own mother says it all isn’t true. Fifteen days out, this is one HELL of an October surprise for Ohio Democrats and Vivek Ramaswamy must be loving it! Acton’s “hard luck” childhood story has been the heart of her campaign pitch since day one! Arthur first disputed Acton’s story back in 2020, when Acton was running Ohio’s COVID response LISTEN TO THE MOM VOTE RED https://t.co/VeTRzxB8BG

“It’s not surprising that Vivek Ramaswamy has stooped to such a despicable low as to attempt to turn the sexual abuse Amy endured at twelve years old from our birth mother’s husband into a political talking point,” Acton’s brother, Philip Stearns, said in a statement.

Amy Acton’s brother slams Vivek Ramaswamy featuring her estranged mother in a campaign ad. "After he was arrested and Amy and I were removed from their custody, our birth mother stayed married to Amy’s rapist until he died. This desperate, disgusting attack reveals exactly who Vivek Ramaswamy is at his core – a pathetic excuse for a man who is willing to hurt anyone as long as it gets him what he wants."

“After he was arrested and Amy and I were removed from their custody, our birth mother stayed married to Amy’s rapist until he died,” Stearns continued. “This desperate, disgusting attack reveals exactly who Vivek Ramaswamy is at his core — a pathetic excuse for a man who is willing to hurt anyone as long as it gets him what he wants.”

The Daily Caller has reached out to Ramaswamy’s campaign. It is unclear whether the campaign had any role in the creation of the video. (RELATED: Is Vivek Ramaswamy The Republicans’ Great Midterm Hope? We Went To Ohio To Find Out)

In a 2019 interview with the Youngstown Vindicator, Acton, then Ohio’s health director under Republican Gov. Mike DeWine, said her childhood was marked by poverty and neglect, and that her mother’s relationships with various men disrupted their family life. news.originalContent:
Photo by Justin Sullivan/Getty Images

Gen Z and millennial customers recorded the fastest growth in credit card spending at Synchrony Financial during the third quarter, the company reported Tuesday, as rising living expenses and elevated borrowing costs strained household budgets.

The lender’s purchase volume climbed 8% to $49.7 billion, with younger consumers driving the strongest growth. The spending increase coincided with mounting affordability pressures, as Federal Reserve research found nearly half of Americans under 30 received financial assistance with expenses in 2025.

Synchrony CEO Brian Doubles said spending increased across generations and credit categories, with the fastest growth among younger customers. The company reported double-digit growth in spending outside its retail partners on both essential and discretionary purchases, including gas stations, electronics and discount stores.

Higher prices themselves contributed to the increase. Synchrony attributed part of its 9% purchase-volume growth in its Home & Auto division and 13% growth in its Diversified & Value division to rising gasoline prices, illustrating how consumers can spend more without necessarily purchasing more goods.

The financial pressures facing younger Americans extend beyond credit cards. A Federal Reserve survey released in May found 47% of adults ages 18 to 29 received help from someone outside their household to cover expenses in 2025, including housing, utilities, transportation and everyday purchases.

The same research found 49% of adults under 30 lived with a parent, up 12 percentage points from 2019. Nearly one-quarter of Americans ages 18 to 29 failed to pay all their bills in full during the month preceding the survey.

Housing affordability compounded the challenge. Home prices increased 54% nationally since 2020, according to Harvard University’s Joint Center for Housing Studies, while nearly half of renter households spent more than 30% of their income on housing at the latest count.

The pressure intensified in September as consumer prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier, while inflation-adjusted average hourly earnings fell 0.7%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. (RELATED: Americans’ Wage Gains Wiped Out By Inflation For 5 Straight Months As Iran War Fallout Continued)

Federal Reserve data also revealed a widening divide between financially comfortable Americans and those struggling to make ends meet. Average credit card balances among respondents who reported difficulty getting by increased 37%, or $2,530, between 2023 and 2025. Balances among those living comfortably increased just 1%, or $59.

Carrying that debt remains expensive. The average interest rate on credit card accounts assessed interest reached 22.36% in August, according to Federal Reserve data. The Fed’s household survey found 46% of credit card holders ages 18 to 29 carried a balance at least once during 2025.

Synchrony’s outstanding loans increased 3% to $103.3 billion in the third quarter, although its delinquency figures offered a more encouraging picture. Loans at least 30 days past due declined to 4.34% from 4.39% a year earlier, while loans at least 90 days past due fell to 2.06% from 2.12%.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Joel Angel Juarez/Getty Images)

Two Democratic areas in Texas posted record-breaking first-day early voting numbers Monday, which could spell trouble for Republicans.

Dallas and Harris County had more voters than ever when early voting began Monday, which was a good sign for Democratic Texas Senate nominee James Talarico. Judge Clay Jenkins, who has access to official data from the Dallas County Elections Department, reported that 76,069 voters showed up in Dallas County, which surpassed the previous record of 60,573 voters in 2020.

The number of registered voters in Dallas surged from 1,398,469 in 2020 to 1,463,708 this year, a 4.7% rise.

Former Vice President Kamala Harris won Dallas County by a 60.1% to 38.1% margin in the 2024 presidential election, according to Politico. Former Democratic Texas Senate nominee Colin Allred won the county by 29 points against Republican Texas Sen. Ted Cruz. (RELATED: Republicans Pour $30,000,000 Into Ken Paxton’s Campaign During Final Stretch Of Red-State Race)

@DallasElections For context the first day vote is up significantly in Dallas County when you compare it to the last Trump midterm in 2018. 2018- 59,388 2026-76,079

The number of voters in Dallas County already surpassed turnout during the 2024 presidential election, according to The Political HQ.

The Harris County Elections Department recorded over 100,000 in-person voters. As of 3:30 pm central time, over 70,000 voters had been processed, which surpassed the previous record of 63,188 votes recorded in the 2018 midterm elections. Harris County includes the city of Houston.

“Harris County has broken the record for first-day early voting turnout in a midterm election!As of 3:30 p.m., 70K+ voters have been processed, surpassing the previous record of 63,188 set in 2018, with 3.5 hours remaining,” the Harris County Elections Department said on X.

Day 1 of Early Voting: As of October 19, 2026, #HarrisCounty has recorded 104.6K + total In-Person Early Voters for the November 3 General & Special Elections. 🗳️✅ #harrisvotes https://t.co/vXRFWBtTSs

The county’s number of registered voters rose 14.7%, from 2,357,199 in 2018 to 2,702,952 this year, according to county data.

Harris won Harris County by a five-point margin, 51.9% to 46.5%, according to Politico.

Over 22,000 voters turned out in El Paso County, the second-highest turnout number on record for the first day of early voting. The historically blue county had its highest ever first-day voter turnout in the 2018 midterm election when 24,449 were recorded. Harris won in El Paso County by 15 points, according to Politico.

Collin County, Denton County and Tarrant County reported increased voter turnout in comparison to the previous election in 2022, which are all historically Republican counties. Collins County reported over 34,000 voters on the first day of early voting, which was well above the roughly 19,000 voters on the first day of early voting in 2022, according to Fox 4 KDFW, a local Fox affiliate.

The county reported approximately 43,000 voters on the first day of early voting in 2024, according to Fox 4 KDFW.

Denton County reported over 34,000 voters on the first day, which surpassed turnout in 2018 and 2022.

Republican PACs spent over $326 million to support Republican Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton while he fell behind Talarico in the polls. Talarico led by an average of 2.2 points as of Tuesday, according to RealClearPolling.

Paxton told donors in leaked audio that the Iran war and gas prices caused his campaign to struggle.

The PACs spent unprecedented amounts in other red states, including Kansas, South Dakota, South Carolina and Iowa.

Below is State of the Day, a morning newsletter from the Daily Caller Editorial Desk. Sign up here.__________

Welcome to State of the Day,

Prepare yourselves; it’ll be a bloodbath for control,

The Conservative Establishment Is Planning For A Post-Trump GOP

More than 500 conservative officials, election administrators, policymakers, and civic leaders.

More than 30 gatherings across 20-plus states. And, for the most part, conversations happening behind closed doors.

That’s the picture Johns Hopkins University’s SNF Agora Institute and the R Street Institute painted in a report published this September, detailing three years of work to build what they call the “Civic Right” — a network of Republicans claiming to be focused on election trust, governing institutions, and the future of their movement.

The initiative’s organizers argue that conservatives need better infrastructure to connect leaders and turn their ideas into sustained political action.

Not exactly the most eye-catching stuff, but it offers a glimpse into the fight over what comes next for the Republican Party, a fight that is playing out beyond the boundaries of Washington’s catfights.

For some, the party’s future means doubling down on Donald Trump’s MAGA movement. For others, it means returning to the old guard of neoconservatism. And for others still, it means turning the page on both and looking for a new cause that’ll resonate with everyday Americans.

Amid all this, the mysterious Civic Right has been meeting privately to discuss what comes next.

The meetings aren’t exactly riveting. There are no stadium rallies, no viral clips, and no grand declaration of war against the current state of the Republican Party.

Instead, there’s an assortment of state officials, local political networks, policy groups, and grant money — the unsightly machinery that shapes politics before any of us even realize it.

The project is led by Scott Warren at Johns Hopkins’ SNF Agora Institute, with R Street’s Matt Germer among its authors. R Street president and co-founder Eli Lehrer came up through the Heritage Foundation, the American Enterprise Institute, and the Heartland Institute, and once wrote speeches for then-Senate Majority Leader Bill Frist.

In other words, this isn’t some grassroots revolt bubbling up from the ranks. It’s an organized effort by longtime center-right policy hands to build a network around their vision.

And there’s money behind the machinery, too. In June 2026, Carnegie Corporation of New York awarded Johns Hopkins $500,000 to support its Conservative Agenda for Democracy program.

Separately, public grant records show that R Street received millions in grants between 2018 and 2025, including $7.1 million from the William and Flora Hewlett Foundation, $2.4 million from the Pew Charitable Trusts, and $935,000 from the Charles Koch Institute.

Charles Koch’s funding network has supported open borders and foreign labor, drawing criticism from both sides of the aisle. In a 2015 interview with Vox, Sen. Bernie Sanders quipped, “Open borders? No, that’s a Koch brothers proposal.”

Sanders went on to correctly argue that businesses benefit from an expanded pool of workers willing to accept rock-bottom wages, which puts pressure on American workers and drives down pay; see cheap foreign labor.

And the Koch brothers aren’t alone. The William and Flora Hewlett Foundation, R Street’s largest reported funder, published a defense of expanded migration, arguing that greater opportunities to move abroad are among the fastest ways to raise living standards.

That’s just a taste of the sort of backers this venture boasts; take all the time you need to really breathe in that ripe swamp stench.

MAGA, on the other hand, offers a different vision, one built around Trump himself. His endorsements, feuds, and demands for loyalty have become defining features of the movement. The populist uprising that promised to take on the establishment has developed its own hierarchy, with Trump at the top.

But with Trump set to leave the presidency after 2028, the movement built around him faces its own identity crisis.

And don’t forget about the disaffected Republicans, as I like to call them, essentially the Thomas Massies and Marjorie Taylor Greenes of the world.

They’re conservatives who don’t neatly fit into either category, but are instead charting a path of their own. A mix of libertarian, conservative, and pragmatic policies makes up the third camp in the war for control.

Who’s to say who’ll come out on top?

The fight won’t just be about who’s the GOP nominee in ‘28; it’s about who has the money, networks, and local infrastructure to turn their vision of the Republican Party into reality.

While everyone argues over the future of the right, some are quietly building it.

How Jared And Ivanka Sparked A Revolution, Daily Caller, John Loftus

The Daily Caller’s John Loftus offers new reporting on the mounting backlash against Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump — along with their political allies in the Albanian government — over a private real estate deal to develop Sazan Island. Riots have broken out in the Albanian capital of Tiranë over what citizens see as a corrupt land deal that has given Kushner and Trump—along with partnered investors—control over the island.

Anthropic Floats Bill That Would Let Feds Step In Only When More Than 50 Lives Are On The Line, Daily Caller News Foundation, Dylan Kresak

Artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic is lobbying Congress to back legislation that would ostensibly limit the Commerce Department’s regulatory oversight of the technology. The Artificial Intelligence Evaluation, Governance, and Incident Safety (AEGIS) Act would only allow federal regulators to step in and shut down an AI model once it has threatened to kill more than 50 people or cause over $1 billion in damage.

Putin Floats a Summit With Trump and Xi to Discuss Ukraine Deal, The Wall Street Journal, Lingling Wei, Alex Leary, Thomas Grove and Josh Dawsey

The Wall Street Journal reported that Vladimir Putin has floated a summit with President Trump and China’s Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The proposal comes as Washington and Beijing are embroiled in a race to lead the AI frontier. The plan could give Beijing a larger role in negotiations on European security, as Putin seeks to capitalize on warming ties with Trump.

Cattle Ranchers Are Getting Grilled 30 Days Into Trump’s Foreign Beef Blitz, Daily Caller, John Loftus

President Donald Trump’s decision to waive tariffs on beef imports from Argentina is costing American ranchers dearly. Just 30 days after the waiver was implemented, “prices paid for live and dressed cutter cows, which compete directly against the lean beef imports, have fallen 12.2 percent and 13.9 percent, respectively,” the watchdog group Farm Action reports. This price drop is significantly affecting American ranchers, who are already hard-pressed by rising diesel prices.

How Jared And Ivanka Sparked A Revolution, Daily Caller, John Loftus

The Daily Caller’s John Loftus offers new reporting on the mounting backlash against Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump — along with their political allies in the Albanian government — over a private real estate deal to develop Sazan Island. Riots have broken out in the Albanian capital of Tiranë over what citizens see as a corrupt land deal that has given Kushner and Trump—along with partnered investors—control over the island.

Anthropic Floats Bill That Would Let Feds Step In Only When More Than 50 Lives Are On The Line, Daily Caller News Foundation, Dylan Kresak

Artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic is lobbying Congress to back legislation that would ostensibly limit the Commerce Department’s regulatory oversight of the technology. The Artificial Intelligence Evaluation, Governance, and Incident Safety (AEGIS) Act would only allow federal regulators to step in and shut down an AI model once it has threatened to kill more than 50 people or cause over $1 billion in damage.

Putin Floats a Summit With Trump and Xi to Discuss Ukraine Deal, The Wall Street Journal, Lingling Wei, Alex Leary, Thomas Grove and Josh Dawsey

The Wall Street Journal reported that Vladimir Putin has floated a summit with President Trump and China’s Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The proposal comes as Washington and Beijing are embroiled in a race to lead the AI frontier. The plan could give Beijing a larger role in negotiations on European security, as Putin seeks to capitalize on warming ties with Trump.

Cattle Ranchers Are Getting Grilled 30 Days Into Trump’s Foreign Beef Blitz, Daily Caller, John Loftus

President Donald Trump’s decision to waive tariffs on beef imports from Argentina is costing American ranchers dearly. Just 30 days after the waiver was implemented, “prices paid for live and dressed cutter cows, which compete directly against the lean beef imports, have fallen 12.2 percent and 13.9 percent, respectively,” the watchdog group Farm Action reports. This price drop is significantly affecting American ranchers, who are already hard-pressed by rising diesel prices.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by NATHAN HOWARD/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Vice President J.D. Vance said Monday he would not endorse Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in an interview with journalist Mark Halperin.

President Donald Trump offered Netanyahu his full endorsement Sunday ahead of Israel’s elections later this month.

“I endorse American candidates, and that’s where I’m focused on is the midterm,” Vance told Halperin aboard Air Force Two. “I’m not getting involved in Israeli elections.”

“I’m not anti-endorsing him. I’m not pro-endorsing him. I’m not getting involved in Israeli elections,” the vice president added.

Netanyahu is facing several challengers this election year, including Gadi Eisenkot, Yair Lapid, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, Yair Golan and Avigdor Liberman, all of whom are members of the opposition bloc. Recent polls show that Eisenkot and the Yashar party have a slight lead over Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party, but neither faction appears to have enough support yet to secure a 61-seat majority in the Knesset.

Trump on Sunday described the Israeli prime minister as a “Great Warrior and an even greater Partner for Peace in combatting [sic] the Islamic Republic of Iran.”

“If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself … This is the kind of Partner that the United States of America is demanding of Israel, a Country for which it has done so much.”

During a recent interview with Fox News host Mark Levin, Netanyahu said that, if he wins re-election, his first goal would be to “achieve the complete elimination of the Iranian threat to Israel, to America, and to the world.” (RELATED: 45 Seconds Into Softball Interview, Netanyahu Tells Mark Levin He Wants To Drag The US Even Deeper Into Iran War)

“This is a regime that chants ‘death to Israel,’ ‘death to America’ — you’re the real target,” Netanyahu told Levin. “I think we are well on our way to achieving this with President Trump’s brilliant leadership, both militarily and then economic blockade, very effective. Let’s complete the job and have the people of Iran seize their own future. It changes the Middle East.”

Vance previously campaigned with Hungary’s then-prime minister, Viktor Orban, in Budapest days before the national election in April, which Orban lost. The vice president said he wanted “to help [Orban] in this campaign cycle” but that the U.S. would “work with whoever wins this election.”

news.originalContent:
ایران می‌گوید قطعنامه نشست سازمان همکاری اسلامی را مصوبه این سازمان تلقی نمی‌کند چون «آیین کار سازمان رعایت نشد.»

این قطعنامه در پایان نشست وزرای خارجه این سازمان که یکشنبه در بغداد به پایان رسید به تصویب رسید.

اسماعیل بقایی، سخنگوی وزارت خارجه ایران، گفت: «مهم‌ترین مصوبه شورای وزیران سازمان همکاری اسلامی در نشست بغداد، بیانیه پایانی است که معمولا با اجماع تصویب می‌شود. آنچه حدود یکی دو ساعت پیش از تصویب بیانیه مطرح شد، این بود که نباید مواردی در متن بیانیه درج شود که موجب تفرقه میان کشورهای اسلامی شود. مشخصا منظور، موضوع یمن بود.»

یکی از قطعنامه‌های صادر شده در این نشست از ایران خواسته است که «به قواعد حقوق بین‌الملل، منشور ملل متحد و کنوانسیون‌های وین درباره روابط دیپلماتیک و کنسولی احترام بگذارد و با نماینده شبه‌نظامیان حوثی در تهران تعامل نکند.»

بند دیگری از این قطعنامه «از همه کشورها می‌خواهد که با نماینده شبه‌نظامیان حوثی در تهران تعامل نکنند، هیچ‌گونه مکاتبه یا معامله‌ای را از جانب او نپذیرند» چون «چنین مکاتبات و معاملاتی باطل و فاقد هرگونه اثر حقوقی هستند.»

این قطعنامه از دولت‌های عضو سازمان همکاری اسلامی خواسته است از تسهیل سفر نماینده حوثی‌ها در تهران خودداری کنند و «در صورت حضور در قلمروشان، او را به دولت جمهوری یمن تحویل دهند.»

ایران از حوثی‌های یمن که در حال مبارزه با ائتلاف به رهبری عربستان سعودی هستند حمایت می‌کند.

نشست وزیران خارجه این سازمان از ۲۵ مهر به مدت دو روز در پایتخت عراق برگزار شد و از ایران عباس عراقچی در آن شرکت کرد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

وزیر خارجه ایران زمانی که برای اجلاس در بغداد بود گفته بود که اگر در بیانیه نهایی اجلاس «انصاف و توازن» رعایت نشود ممکن است ایران آن را قبول نکند.

او پیش‌بینی کرده بود که «تقریبا اکثر قریب به اتفاق قطعنامه‌ها تکرار سال گذشته» باشد اما در مورد یمن «بحث‌های جدی صورت گرفت. سعودی‌ها نظرات خودشان را داشتند، ما هم نظراتمان را بیان کردیم. کشورهای دیگر هم به همین ترتیب.»

آقای عراقچی همچنین گفت که «بلوک کشورهای نزدیک به مواضع عربستان» در سازمان همکاری اسلامی «قابل توجه» است و «این واقعیتی است که باید در نظر داشته باشیم.»

او گفت که ایران «لابی‌های گسترده‌ای» انجام داده است و اظهار امیدواری کرد که در بیانیه نهایی اجلاس «انصاف و توازن» رعایت شود، در غیر این صورت «جمهوری اسلامی ایران نمی‌تواند به آنها بپیوندد و حتما خودش را از قطعنامه‌های صادره یا آن قطعنامه خاص جدا خواهد کرد، تحفظ [پرهیز] خواهیم کرد. حتی ممکن است که صراحتا اعلام کنیم که قبول نداریم.»

این پنجاه‌ودومین نشست شورای وزیران امور خارجه کشورهای عضو سازمان همکاری‌های اسلامی بود که در سایه جنگ و تنش در منطقه برگزار شد.

news.title: مهدی خان‌بابا تهرانی، از چهره‌های سرشناس جنبش چپ ایران، درگذشت
news.originalSummary:
منبع تصویر، khanbabatehrani.com

مهدی خان‌بابا تهرانی، از چهره‌های باسابقه جنبش چپ ایران و فعالان سیاسی و دانشجویی پیش از انقلاب ۱۳۵۷، شامگاه دوشنبه ۲۷ مهر در ۹۲سالگی در فرانکفورت آلمان درگذشت.

او که سال‌ها در جریان‌های مختلف چپ فعالیت داشت، در دهه‌های پایانی زندگی به بازنگری در اندیشه‌ها و تجربه‌های سیاسی گذشته خود پرداخت و به دفاع از دموکراسی و تقویت جامعه مدنی روی آورد.
